gates.reason: Parses sensitive local experiment text without filesystem access, network/LLM egress, command execution, HTML rendering, or secret handling.

Checked disposition reconciliation, provenance classification, live-trust gating, bounded variation identities, proof freshness, paired arithmetic, stable summation, and evidence formatting; no reproducible defect survived review.
Aggregation is linear-pass processing with bounded source/variation cardinality and bounded normalized receipt buffering; no release-blocking hotspot was verified.
Pure parser tests contain no security boundary, filesystem operation, egress, rendering, command execution, or secret handling.
The test at line 100 codifies missing activity measurements as zero, allowing absent evidence to become a reproducible activity claim.
Unit-test fixtures do not implement a production hot path or performance surface.
The SPA-capable parser only decodes data and performs arithmetic; it has no filesystem access, egress, HTML injection sink, command execution, or secret handling.
Lines 92-99 accept unvalidated dates and replace absent/invalid measurements with zero; lines 185-190 also treat an invalid lastComputedDate as fresh because NaN never satisfies the stale comparison.
Parsing, sorting, and trend calculation are straightforward over daily rows with no repeated per-row recomputation beyond one sort and linear reductions.
Filesystem operations are confined to uniquely created temporary directories and fixed child filenames, with cleanup limited to those recorded directories.
Tests cover sanitization, malformed-line rejection, event counts, tag taxonomy, deterministic ordering, zero-denominator handling, and file-read failure behavior.
The unit tests do not ship a production hot path or introduce a performance-sensitive surface.
The reader performs read-only access to the caller-supplied path and has no write, traversal construction, egress, rendering sink, command execution, or secret transmission.
Checked fail-closed record validation, timestamp normalization, event/tag allowlists, count arithmetic, latest-time selection, deterministic sorting, and the zero-denominator rate guard.
Per-line byte bounds and single aggregation passes limit per-record work; no repeated per-rule rescans or other release-blocking recomputation was found.

findings.title: Malformed or missing stats-cache fields are converted into fresh zero-activity evidence
findings.where: src/lib/parse-stats-cache.ts:92-99 and 185-190; behavior is explicitly asserted by src/lib/parse-stats-cache.test.ts:100-111.
findings.what: Any string is accepted as a daily date, missing or invalid numeric measurements are replaced with 0, and any non-empty lastComputedDate is accepted. Consequently a partial row becomes claimed zero activity, while an invalid lastComputedDate produces NaN and leaves stale=false. Both outcomes turn absent or malformed artifact evidence into affirmative trend/freshness claims.
findings.fix: Strictly validate YYYY-MM-DD dates and finite non-negative activity counts. Reject incomplete malformed rows (or represent measurements as unknown) instead of defaulting them to zero, and reject the cache or force stale=true when lastComputedDate cannot be parsed.
findings.acceptance: Add tests proving that malformed dates, invalid/negative counts, and missing measurements cannot contribute zero-valued trend evidence, and that an invalid lastComputedDate cannot yield stale=false; retain passing arithmetic tests for complete valid fixtures.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed safeDailyActivity accepts every string date and substitutes 0 for each invalid measurement at lines 92-99; the existing test requires that substitution at lines 100-111. Re-reading lines 185-190 confirmed Date parsing can return NaN and `nowMs - NaN > TWO_DAYS_MS` is false, reproducibly reporting malformed freshness metadata as not stale.
